# kopia_notification_profile (Resource)

Manages a Kopia notification profile: a destination — email, [Pushover](https://pushover.net) or a webhook — to which the Kopia server sends its notifications, such as snapshot reports, from a minimum severity on. Exactly one of `email`, `pushover` and `webhook` must be set; moving from one to another changes the profile in place.

Kopia keeps profiles in the repository, so the server needs one connected, and applies a change to the next notification without a restart. Kopia checks nothing when it saves a profile — an invalid one is stored, and then silently skipped whenever a notification goes out — so the provider validates every setting at plan time, and `send_test_on_apply` proves that delivery works.

Creating a profile under a name that already exists fails, because Kopia would overwrite it without a word: import the existing profile instead. Destroying the resource deletes the profile. Template overrides made for it with `kopia notification template set` are not deleted with it, and apply again to a profile created later under the same name.

~> **Secrets are stored in state.** Kopia returns every setting whenever a profile is read — SMTP password, Pushover tokens, webhook URL and headers included — so they are kept in Terraform state, and changes made outside Terraform show up as drift. They are marked sensitive. Kopia itself also writes a saved profile's settings, secrets included, to its log files at debug level, the level those files record by default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A webhook to an ntfy topic. Kopia counts only HTTP 200 as delivered: ntfy
# answers 200, but a service that answers 201, 202 or 204 makes every
# notification fail.
resource "kopia_notification_profile" "ntfy" {
  name         = "ntfy"
  min_severity = "warning"

  webhook = {
    endpoint = "https://ntfy.example.org/kopia-backups"
    headers = {
      Authorization = "Bearer ${var.ntfy_token}"
      Priority      = "high"
    }
  }

  # Have Kopia send its test notification after every apply that creates or
  # changes the profile, so that a wrong token fails the apply rather than the
  # next real report. Every test delivers a real message.
  send_test_on_apply = true
}

# Email through a submission server. Kopia connects without encryption and
# switches to TLS with STARTTLS when the server offers it; implicit TLS on port
# 465 does not work.
resource "kopia_notification_profile" "mail" {
  name = "mail"

  email = {
    smtp_server   = "smtp.example.com"
    smtp_port     = 587
    smtp_username = "kopia@example.com"
    smtp_password = var.smtp_password
    from          = "kopia@example.com"
    # Bare addresses separated by commas, without spaces. Kopia ignores `cc`,
    # so every recipient goes here.
    to = "ops@example.com,oncall@example.com"
  }
}

# Pushover, for errors only. `format` is "txt" (the default here) or "html";
# Kopia accepts no other value, "md" included.
resource "kopia_notification_profile" "phone" {
  name         = "phone"
  min_severity = "error"

  pushover = {
    app_token = var.pushover_app_token
    user_key  = var.pushover_user_key
    format    = "html"
  }
}

variable "ntfy_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "pushover_app_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "pushover_user_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the profile, unique on the server and case-sensitive. It must not be empty, contain `/`, or be `.` or `..`: Kopia would store such a profile, but could then neither read nor delete it. Changing it replaces the profile.

### Optional

- `email` (Attributes) Send notifications by email. Kopia uses Go's `net/smtp`: it connects without encryption and switches to TLS with STARTTLS when the server offers it, verifying the server's certificate against the system's trusted roots. There is no implicit TLS, so SMTPS on port 465 does not work, and no setting to skip certificate verification. Kopia sends the password only over TLS, or to a server at `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--email))
- `min_severity` (String) Lowest severity of the notifications the profile receives. Defaults to `report`, as for a profile made with `kopia notification profile configure`. Kopia's severities, from the lowest, are `verbose`, `success`, `report`, `warning` and `error`. The server's scheduler sends a snapshot report as `report`, or as `warning` or `error` when the snapshot had problems; nothing Kopia sends today is below `report` except the test notification, which ignores this setting, so `verbose`, `success` and `report` currently behave the same. Kopia's API accepts any number here: one that has no name is shown as the number, such as `"3"`. Such a number is replaced on the next apply.
- `pushover` (Attributes) Send notifications through [Pushover](https://pushover.net). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--pushover))
- `send_test_on_apply` (Boolean) Have Kopia send its test notification through the profile after every apply that creates or changes it, so that a wrong setting fails the apply rather than the next real notification. Defaults to `false`. Turning it on changes nothing in Kopia and sends nothing by itself, and every test delivers a real message.

Kopia waits for delivery without an overall time limit of its own — for email, without any — so the provider's `request_timeout` bounds the test; when it expires, the outcome is unknown and the message may still arrive. A failed test fails the apply, but the profile has been saved: after a create, Terraform marks it tainted and replaces it, testing again, on the next apply; after an update, the next apply tests again only if the profile changes again.
- `webhook` (Attributes) Send notifications as HTTP requests. The body is the rendered message, without a `Content-Type` header unless `headers` sets one, and the subject goes in a `Subject` header. Kopia sends from the server, honouring the proxy variables in its environment and following redirects.

~> **Only HTTP 200 counts as delivered.** A service that answers 201, 202 or 204 makes every notification fail. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--webhook))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

<a id="nestedatt--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `email`

Required:

- `from` (String) Sender address, used for the envelope and the `From:` header: a bare address such as `kopia@example.com`. Kopia hands it to the SMTP server as it is, so a display name such as `Kopia <kopia@example.com>` does not work.
- `smtp_server` (String) Host name or IP address of the SMTP server, without a port.
- `to` (String) Recipients: bare addresses separated by commas without spaces, such as `ops@example.com,oncall@example.com`. Kopia splits the list at the commas and hands each part to the SMTP server as it is.

Optional:

- `cc` (String) Copy recipients, in the same form as `to`.

~> **Has no effect.** Kopia stores this setting, but its email sender neither sends to these addresses nor adds a `Cc:` header. It is offered only so that a profile set up elsewhere can be managed as it is.
- `format` (String) Message format: `txt` or `html`. Defaults to `html`. Kopia accepts no other value — its code comments mention `md`, but its senders refuse it — and picks the matching template, plain text or HTML.
- `smtp_identity` (String) Authorisation identity for SMTP PLAIN authentication, which almost every server leaves empty. Leave it out for none. Requires `smtp_username`.
- `smtp_password` (String, Sensitive) Password to authenticate with. Leave it out for none. Requires `smtp_username`.
- `smtp_port` (Number) Port of the SMTP server. Defaults to `587`, the submission port.
- `smtp_username` (String) User name to authenticate with. Leave it out to send without authentication; when it is set, the server must offer SMTP authentication.


<a id="nestedatt--pushover"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pushover`

Required:

- `app_token` (String, Sensitive) API token of the Pushover application to send as.
- `user_key` (String, Sensitive) Key of the Pushover user or group to send to.

Optional:

- `endpoint` (String) URL of the Pushover message API. Leave it out for Pushover's own, `https://api.pushover.net/1/messages.json`. Kopia keeps this setting for its tests and its CLI does not offer it; set it only for a service that implements the same API.
- `format` (String) Message format: `txt` or `html`. Defaults to `txt`. Kopia accepts no other value — its code comments mention `md`, but its senders refuse it — and picks the matching template, plain text or HTML.


<a id="nestedatt--webhook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `webhook`

Required:

- `endpoint` (String, Sensitive) URL to send to, `http://` or `https://`. It is sensitive because services such as Slack, Discord or ntfy put their token in the URL.

Optional:

- `format` (String) Message format: `txt` or `html`. Defaults to `txt`. Kopia accepts no other value — its code comments mention `md`, but its senders refuse it — and picks the matching template, plain text or HTML.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Extra request headers, by name, such as `{ Authorization = "Bearer …" }`. Names must be HTTP tokens and unique regardless of letter case; values must not contain line breaks or other control characters, or begin or end with whitespace. A `Subject` header replaces the subject Kopia sets. Kopia stores the headers as one `Name: value` line each, which the provider writes sorted by name. Leave it out for none.
- `method` (String) HTTP method, in upper case. Defaults to `POST`; Kopia's CLI offers `POST` and `PUT`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = kopia_notification_profile.ntfy
  identity = {
    name = "ntfy"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the notification profile.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = kopia_notification_profile.ntfy
  id = "ntfy"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Notification profiles are imported by name, as `kopia notification profile
# list` or the kopia_notification_profiles data source shows it. Names are
# case-sensitive. Kopia returns every setting, secrets included, so nothing is
# lost on import, and the first plan shows any difference from the
# configuration.
terraform import kopia_notification_profile.ntfy ntfy
```
